go:github.com/riducms/ridu/store#Value.G.summary: Read an immutable object child without copying its container.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: A literal direct-child name; dots do not traverse nested objects.

returns.description: The child value, or Null for a missing key or a non-object.

details: Use Lookup when missing and explicit null must be distinguished.
go:github.com/riducms/ridu/store#Value.G.example:
seo := store.Object(store.Values{"title": store.String("Home")})
title, ok := seo.Get("title").StringValue()

go:github.com/riducms/ridu/store#Value.L.summary: Read an immutable object child and report whether the key exists.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: A literal direct-child name; dots do not traverse nested objects.

returns.description: The child and true when the key exists, including explicit Null; false for a missing key or a non-object.

go:github.com/riducms/ridu/store#Value.E.summary: Iterate immutable object members without copying the map.

returns.description: An iterator yielding each direct-child name and value, in unspecified order.

details: Non-objects yield no entries. The iterator keeps its snapshot and can be reused, including after an early stop.

go:github.com/riducms/ridu/store#Value.E.summary: Iterate immutable list items in order without making a slice.

returns.description: An iterator over the list items in their stored order.

details: Non-lists yield no elements. The iterator keeps its snapshot and can be reused, including after an early stop.

go:github.com/riducms/ridu/store#Value.L.summary: Count direct object members or list items without copying.

returns.description: The number of members or items, or zero for other kinds.

details: Use Kind when an empty container must be distinguished from a scalar.

go:github.com/riducms/ridu/store#Value.L.summary: Read one immutable list item without copying the list.

returns.description: The item and true, or false for a non-list or an out-of-range index.

go:github.com/riducms/ridu/store#Value.W.summary: Replace one list item while sharing unchanged immutable items.

returns.description: The updated list and true, or the original value and false for a non-list or an out-of-range index.

details: The original list and retained snapshots are unchanged. Use List to change list length or order.

go:github.com/riducms/ridu/store#Value.C.summary: Create a mutable copy of an object field map.

returns.description: A detached field map and a boolean reporting whether the value is an object.

details: Child Values remain immutable. Use Get, Lookup or Entries when only reading.
go:github.com/riducms/ridu/store#Value.C.example:
seo := store.Object(store.Values{"title": store.String("Home")})
fields, ok := seo.CopyObject()
if ok {
	fields["title"] = store.String("Welcome")
	updated := store.Object(fields)
	fmt.Println(updated.Get("title"))
}

go:github.com/riducms/ridu/store#Value.C.summary: Create a mutable slice containing the list items.

returns.description: A detached slice and a boolean reporting whether the value is a list.

details: Child Values remain immutable. Use Elements or ListItem for reads, and WithListItem for a single replacement.

go:github.com/riducms/ridu/store#Value.C.summary: Copy a populated document for editing or interoperability.

returns.description: A detached document and true when populated; otherwise an empty document and false.

details: Metadata and field maps are copied. Child Values remain immutable.

go:github.com/riducms/ridu/store#Value.S.summary: Recognize retained immutable sources before repeating derived work.

parameters.name: other
parameters.description: Another retained immutable value to compare with the receiver.

returns.description: True for shared container backing or exactly matching scalar values; false for different kinds or backing.

details: This checks source identity without traversing container contents. Separately constructed containers can return false even when their serialized contents match.
Scalar numbers compare their bits, so positive and negative zero differ. Empty lists share their empty backing.
Keep caches bounded and retain their source Values. Retaining a source also retains the immutable data reachable from it.
